cls: Bismuth-based mucosal protectant and anti-Helicobacter agent (cytoprotective antiulcer drug)
pharm: Bismuth salt that forms a protective coagulum over ulcer craters, stimulates mucosal defenses, and has direct bactericidal activity against Helicobacter pylori.
quick: 120 mg (as bismuth oxide) four times daily, or 240 mg twice daily, before meals and at bedtime
Take 30 minutes before meals; avoid milk/antacids around dosing
Contraindicated in moderate-to-severe renal impairment (bismuth accumulation)
Symptom relief; limit course duration to avoid bismuth toxicity
summary: Colloidal bismuth subcitrate (tripotassium dicitratobismuthate) is a bismuth-based antiulcer agent used to heal gastric and duodenal ulcers and, importantly, as part of bismuth-containing quadruple therapy to eradicate Helicobacter pylori. In the acidic stomach it forms an insoluble protective layer over the ulcer base, stimulates mucosal prostaglandins, bicarbonate, and epidermal growth factor, and exerts direct bactericidal activity against H. pylori while preventing its adhesion to gastric epithelium. The usual regimen is 120 mg four times daily or 240 mg twice daily for a limited course (typically up to 4-8 weeks). It commonly blackens the stool and tongue (harmless) and is contraindicated in significant renal impairment because of the risk of bismuth accumulation and neurotoxicity. It should be separated from food, milk, and antacids. It is not FDA-approved (data from EMA/BNF; in the US, bismuth subsalicylate is the marketed bismuth salt).
indications: Healing of benign gastric and duodenal ulcers
Eradication of Helicobacter pylori as part of bismuth-containing combination (quadruple) therapy
Symptomatic relief and prevention of relapse in peptic ulcer disease

dosage.d: 120 mg (as bismuth oxide) four times daily (before the three main meals and at bedtime), or 240 mg twice daily, for 4-8 weeks
dosage.t: Four times daily or twice daily
dosage.n: Take 30 minutes before meals; do not exceed an 8-week continuous course

dosage.d: 120 mg (bismuth oxide) four times daily combined with a proton pump inhibitor and two antibiotics (e.g., tetracycline + metronidazole) for 10-14 days
Do not use continuously beyond 8 weeks; allow a bismuth-free interval before repeating

admin: Take 30 minutes before meals (and at bedtime for the four-times-daily regimen) on an empty stomach
Avoid food, milk/dairy, and antacids within 30 minutes before or after a dose (they reduce efficacy)
Do not exceed the recommended course duration (typically up to 8 weeks)
Inform the patient that stools and tongue may turn black/dark - this is harmless and reversible
Use combination regimens (PPI plus antibiotics) for H. pylori eradication
moa: Colloidal bismuth subcitrate acts through several complementary mechanisms. In the acidic gastric environment it precipitates to form an insoluble bismuth-protein coagulum that selectively coats the base of ulcer craters, providing a physical protective barrier against acid, pepsin, and bile. It stimulates mucosal defence by increasing local prostaglandin, bicarbonate, and mucus secretion and by promoting accumulation of epidermal growth factor at the ulcer margin, accelerating healing. It also has direct bactericidal activity against Helicobacter pylori - inhibiting bacterial protein and cell-wall synthesis, membrane function, and ATP production - and prevents adhesion of H. pylori to gastric epithelial cells, which underlies its role in eradication therapy.

absolute: Moderate to severe renal impairment (risk of bismuth accumulation and encephalopathy)
relative: Prolonged or repeated courses (cumulative bismuth exposure)
monitor: Course duration and cumulative bismuth exposure
Neurological symptoms with prolonged/high-dose use (bismuth encephalopathy)

preg: There are limited data; avoid colloidal bismuth subcitrate during pregnancy unless clearly necessary, owing to potential bismuth absorption and lack of safety data.
lact: Use is best avoided during breastfeeding because of limited data on bismuth excretion into milk and potential infant exposure.
renal: Contraindicated in moderate to severe renal impairment because bismuth is excreted renally and can accumulate, raising the risk of bismuth toxicity, including reversible encephalopathy.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; specific dose-adjustment data are limited.

moderate: Tetracyclines - bismuth reduces their absorption; separate dosing (though they are deliberately combined within eradication regimens with timing guidance)
Antacids, milk/dairy, and other polyvalent cations - reduce bismuth efficacy; separate from dosing
minor: Other oral drugs - may have reduced absorption if taken together; separate administration
interactions.food: Take 30 minutes before meals; food, milk, and antacids reduce its protective and antibacterial effect.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol, which can aggravate peptic ulceration.
interactions.diagnostics: Bismuth is radiopaque and may interfere with imaging/endoscopic interpretation; blackening of stool can mimic melaena and may affect faecal occult blood tests.

serious: Bismuth encephalopathy with prolonged/excessive use (confusion, ataxia, myoclonus)
rare: Reversible neurotoxicity (historical, with high cumulative doses)
emergency: Neurological deterioration suggesting bismuth encephalopathy (confusion, tremor, ataxia, myoclonus)

monitoring: Limit course duration (avoid continuous use beyond 8 weeks)
Neurological status with prolonged or repeated courses
Stool colour change (expected; distinguish from GI bleeding clinically)
counsel: Take this medicine on an empty stomach, about 30 minutes before meals
Do not take milk, dairy, or antacids close to your dose - they stop it working properly
Your stools and tongue may turn black; this is harmless and goes away after you stop
Do not take it continuously for longer than your doctor advises (usually up to 8 weeks)
Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems before taking this medicine
If you are being treated for H. pylori, complete the full course of all the medicines together
pk: Local protective action begins on contact with the gastric mucosa
Minimal systemic absorption of bismuth (small fraction absorbed)
Absorbed bismuth has a long terminal elimination half-life (days to weeks); excreted renally
Local effect during dosing intervals; given 2-4 times daily
Store below 25 C; protect from light and moisture
pearls: Acts locally by coating ulcer craters AND has direct bactericidal action against H. pylori - key component of bismuth quadruple therapy
Take 30 minutes before meals on an empty stomach; keep away from food, milk, and antacids
Harmless black stools and dark tongue are expected - reassure patients (may mimic melaena)
Contraindicated in moderate-to-severe renal impairment due to bismuth accumulation and encephalopathy risk
Limit to short courses (up to ~8 weeks) to avoid cumulative bismuth toxicity
Not FDA-approved (tripotassium dicitratobismuthate); used in EU/UK and elsewhere - in the US bismuth subsalicylate is the marketed salt
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose. Do not take a double dose. Try to keep doses about 30 minutes before meals.
overdose: Acute overdose may cause gastrointestinal upset (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain). Chronic excessive intake can lead to bismuth accumulation with nephrotoxicity and reversible bismuth encephalopathy (confusion, tremor, ataxia, myoclonus). Management is supportive, stopping the drug; gastric lavage may be considered after very large recent ingestion, renal function should be monitored, and chelation may be considered for severe systemic bismuth toxicity under specialist guidance.
